review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

2:1.sourceText: Ἐρωτῶμεν δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, ὑπὲρ τῆς παρουσίας τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἡμῶν ἐπισυναγωγῆς ἐπ’ αὐτόν,
2:1.targetText: And we ask you, brothers, in regard to the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and of our gathering together to Him,

2:2.sourceText: εἰς τὸ μὴ ταχέως σαλευθῆναι ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ νοὸς μηδὲ θροεῖσθαι μήτε διὰ πνεύματος μήτε διὰ λόγου μήτε δι’ ἐπιστολῆς ὡς δι’ ἡμῶν, ὡς ὅτι ἐνέστηκεν ἡ ἡμέρα τοῦ Κυρίου.
2:2.targetText: that you are not quickly shaken in mind, nor be troubled, neither through spirit, neither through word, neither through letters as through us, as that the Day of the LORD has arrived;

groups.note: The Greek phrase ἀπὸ τοῦ νοός means away from/out of ones settled understanding. LSV recasts the disturbance as shaken in mind; the whole phrase is linked without making ἀπό and in general lexical synonyms.
Both N1904 and TR have singular ἐπιστολῆς, letter; LSV prints plural letters. The shared letter noun is retained with its English number difference explicit.

2:3.sourceText: μή τις ὑμᾶς ἐξαπατήσῃ κατὰ μηδένα τρόπον· ὅτι ἐὰν μὴ ἔλθῃ ἡ ἀποστασία πρῶτον καὶ ἀποκαλυφθῇ ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῆς ἀνομίας, ὁ υἱὸς τῆς ἀπωλείας,
2:3.targetText: do not let anyone deceive you in any way, because if the departure may not come first, the man of lawlessness may [not] be revealed—the son of destruction,

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 καί coordinates the departure and revelation within the unless condition. LSV prints an asyndetic conditional/revelation sequence; there is no and at this point and καί is not falsely assigned to the bracketed second negative.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English negative supplied by LSV in the revelation clause. Greek has only the earlier μή within ἐὰν μή; that actual token stays linked to the first unbracketed not, rather than being duplicated to imply identical conditional syntax.

review.note: N1904 coordinates departure and revelation under an ἐὰν μή/unless construction. LSV prints if the departure may not come first, the man ... may [not] be revealed, including a second bracketed negative. The review preserves the actual LSV reading and lexical heads without claiming identical logical syntax or inventing a second Greek negative.

2:4.sourceText: ὁ ἀντικείμενος καὶ ὑπεραιρόμενος ἐπὶ πάντα λεγόμενον Θεὸν ἢ σέβασμα, ὥστε αὐτὸν εἰς τὸν ναὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ καθίσαι, ἀποδεικνύντα ἑαυτὸν ὅτι ἔστιν Θεός.
2:4.targetText: who is opposing and is raising himself up above all called god or worshiped, so as for him to have sat down in the temple of God, proclaiming that he is God.

groups.note: The middle raising-oneself participle ὑπεραιρόμενος supplies the reflexive English himself; there is no separate Greek reflexive at that first occurrence.

σέβασμα is a thing/object of worship; LSV expresses this second class of revered objects by the participial worshiped in all called god or worshiped. This noun-to-predicate recast is contextual, not a claim that the Greek is a passive worship verb.
N1904 εἰς marks the direction into the temple; LSV renders the seating location in the temple. The actual directional/location relation is retained without equating every εἰς with in.
The aorist infinitive καθίσαι is rendered to have sat down; the English have belongs to its aspect phrasing and is not a separate Greek possession verb.

ἀποδεικνύντα ἑαυτὸν ὅτι ἔστιν, displaying/showing himself that he is, is rendered proclaiming that he is. The reflexive object of the display is absorbed into the same-person subject of the English claim clause, so the full constituent is kept together.

2:5.sourceText: Οὐ μνημονεύετε ὅτι ἔτι ὢν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ταῦτα ἔλεγον ὑμῖν;
2:5.targetText: Do you not remember that, yet being with you, I said these things to you?

2:6.sourceText: καὶ νῦν τὸ κατέχον οἴδατε, εἰς τὸ ἀποκαλυφθῆναι αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ αὐτοῦ καιρῷ.
2:6.targetText: And now, you have known what is restraining, for his being revealed in his own time,

groups.note: The accusative subject αὐτόν of the infinitive being revealed is rendered as possessive his before the English gerund. The same revealed person is retained through the grammatical recast.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV own follows TR reflexive ἑαυτοῦ, whereas pinned N1904 has simple third-person αὐτοῦ. The actual his stays linked without inventing a separate own word.

2:7.sourceText: τὸ γὰρ μυστήριον ἤδη ἐνεργεῖται τῆς ἀνομίας· μόνον ὁ κατέχων ἄρτι ἕως ἐκ μέσου γένηται.
2:7.targetText: for the secret of lawlessness already works, only the [One] now restraining [will do so] until He may come out of [the] midst,

groups.note: The idiom ἐκ μέσου γένηται, become out of the midst/out of the way, is rendered He may come out of [the] midst. The whole exit/removal-from-the-midst constituent is linked; this is not a claim that γίνομαι generally means come on a journey.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English predicate completes the elliptical only the One now restraining clause; there is no additional Greek future doing verb.
Bracketed English article supplied with midst; Greek μέσου has no separate article here.

2:8.sourceText: καὶ τότε ἀποκαλυφθήσεται ὁ ἄνομος, ὃν ὁ Κύριος Ἰησοῦς ἀνελεῖ τῷ πνεύματι τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ καὶ καταργήσει τῇ ἐπιφανείᾳ τῆς παρουσίας αὐτοῦ,
2:8.targetText: and then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the LORD will consume with the Spirit of His mouth, and will nullify at the appearance of His coming,

groups.note: N1904 ἀνελεῖ denotes kill/destroy, while LSV consume follows TR ἀναλώσει. In this judgment context consume denotes destroying the lawless one, so the shared destructive action is linked with the different Greek verb reading explicit; no general kill/eat lexical equation is implied.

unmappedSource.reason: Source-witness title difference: N1904 explicitly has Jesus after Lord, absent from the LSV/TR title at this point.

2:9.sourceText: οὗ ἐστιν ἡ παρουσία κατ’ ἐνέργειαν τοῦ Σατανᾶ ἐν πάσῃ δυνάμει καὶ σημείοις καὶ τέρασιν ψεύδους
2:9.targetText: whose coming is according to the working of Satan, in all power, and signs, and lying wonders,

groups.note: τέρασιν ψεύδους, wonders of falsehood, is rendered lying wonders; the genitive falsehood noun becomes an English adjective in the whole noun phrase.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

2:10.sourceText: καὶ ἐν πάσῃ ἀπάτῃ ἀδικίας τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις, ἀνθ’ ὧν τὴν ἀγάπην τῆς ἀληθείας οὐκ ἐδέξαντο εἰς τὸ σωθῆναι αὐτούς.
2:10.targetText: and in all deceitfulness of the unrighteousness in those perishing, because they did not receive the love of the truth for their being saved,

groups.note: Greek accusative αὐτούς supplies the subject of the passive articular infinitive; English renders this as their before being saved, with the same recipients.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness preposition difference: TR explicitly has ἐν before the perishing people, behind LSV in those perishing; N1904 has a bare dative τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις at this point.

2:11.sourceText: καὶ διὰ τοῦτο πέμπει αὐτοῖς ὁ Θεὸς ἐνέργειαν πλάνης εἰς τὸ πιστεῦσαι αὐτοὺς τῷ ψεύδει,
2:11.targetText: and because of this God will send to them a working of delusion, for their believing the lie,

groups.note: N1904 πέμπει is present sends; LSV will send follows TR future πέμψει. The same sending verb is linked with the tense difference explicit.
The accusative subject αὐτούς of the articular infinitive is expressed as their before the English gerund believing, without a different person/reference.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

2:12.sourceText: ἵνα κριθῶσιν πάντες οἱ μὴ πιστεύσαντες τῇ ἀληθείᾳ ἀλλὰ εὐδοκήσαντες τῇ ἀδικίᾳ.
2:12.targetText: that they may be judged—all who did not believe the truth, but were well pleased in the unrighteousness.

groups.note: The dative noun phrase τῇ ἀδικίᾳ is rendered in the unrighteousness as the sphere/object of their pleasure; in belongs to the case construction, not a separate Greek preposition.

2:13.sourceText: Ἡμεῖς δὲ ὀφείλομεν εὐχαριστεῖν τῷ Θεῷ πάντοτε περὶ ὑμῶν, ἀδελφοὶ ἠγαπημένοι ὑπὸ Κυρίου, ὅτι εἵλατο ὑμᾶς ὁ Θεὸς ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς εἰς σωτηρίαν ἐν ἁγιασμῷ Πνεύματος καὶ πίστει ἀληθείας,
2:13.targetText: And we ought to give thanks to God always for you, brothers, beloved by the LORD, that God chose you from the beginning to salvation, in sanctification of the Spirit, and belief of the truth,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

2:14.sourceText: εἰς ὃ καὶ ἐκάλεσεν ὑμᾶς διὰ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ἡμῶν, εἰς περιποίησιν δόξης τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
2:14.targetText: to which He called you through our good news, to the acquiring of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ;

unmappedSource.reason: Source-witness connective difference: N1904 has καί also before He called; LSV/TR has no separate also at this point.
The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

2:15.sourceText: Ἄρα οὖν, ἀδελφοί, στήκετε, καὶ κρατεῖτε τὰς παραδόσεις ἃς ἐδιδάχθητε εἴτε διὰ λόγου εἴτε δι’ ἐπιστολῆς ἡμῶν.
2:15.targetText: so, then, brothers, stand fast, and hold the traditions that you were taught, whether through word, whether through our letter;

2:16.sourceText: Αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ Κύριος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς καὶ ὁ Θεὸς ὁ Πατὴρ ἡμῶν, ὁ ἀγαπήσας ἡμᾶς καὶ δοὺς παράκλησιν αἰωνίαν καὶ ἐλπίδα ἀγαθὴν ἐν χάριτι,
2:16.targetText: and may our Lord Jesus Christ Himself, and our God and Father, who loved us, and gave continuous comfort, and good hope in grace,

groups.note: Split English auxiliary across verse references: may at LSV2:16 expresses the optative mood of both actual Greek2:17 verbs παρακαλέσαι and στηρίξαι. Those same original word identities also anchor their lexical English heads comfort/establish in2:17. This is a genuine one-to-many cross-reference rendering, not movement or invented source words.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness/apposition difference: N1904 has God the Father, while LSV our God and Father follows TR with an additional coordinating καί. The real God/Father words and shared possessive stay linked.

2:17.sourceText: παρακαλέσαι ὑμῶν τὰς καρδίας καὶ στηρίξαι ἐν παντὶ ἔργῳ καὶ λόγῳ ἀγαθῷ.
2:17.targetText: comfort your hearts, and establish you in every good word and work.

groups.note: This optative comfort verb supplies lexical comfort here and, together with στηρίξαι, the English wish-auxiliary may placed in LSV2:16. The same actual source identity legitimately has counterparts in both English references.

This coordinated optative establish verb supplies lexical establish here and shares its preceding English may in LSV2:16. The explicit foreign group there uses these same source indices, not an invented extra Greek auxiliary.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness object difference: LSV you after establish follows additional TR ὑμᾶς. N1904 has no separate you object after στηρίξαι; its earlier ὑμῶν remains linked to your hearts.
